questions.q: Why does GPU capacity planning start with checking quota, before writing any Terraform?
options: Terraform cannot create GPU resources on Azure or AWS under any circumstances
Quota checks are only required for spot/low-priority GPU instances, never on-demand ones
Subscriptions and accounts often have a very low or zero default quota for GPU VM families per region, so a correct Terraform config can still fail to apply
GPU VMs do not use the standard vCPU quota system at all
questions.explain: GPU families frequently ship with a default quota of zero per region. A perfectly valid terraform apply can still fail on a quota/capacity error if that hasn't been raised first, and quota is scoped per region.

questions.q: In the azurerm_linux_virtual_machine resource block for an NC A100 v4 GPU VM, which argument determines that it's a GPU VM at all?
options: The size argument, set to a value like "Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4"
A separate gpu_enabled = true argument on the resource
The resource_group_name argument
The admin_ssh_key block
questions.explain: There's no separate GPU flag — the VM size itself (e.g. Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4) is what determines whether the VM has a GPU attached. The resource type is the same azurerm_linux_virtual_machine used for any VM.

questions.q: What does AWS's p4d.24xlarge instance type provide?
options: A single NVIDIA V100 GPU with no NVLink
A CPU-only instance tuned for high memory bandwidth
8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs, AWS's current flagship training instance
8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs connected via NVLink, a mainstream multi-GPU training instance
questions.explain: p4d.24xlarge provides 8 A100 GPUs with NVLink interconnect between them. p5.48xlarge is the 8x H100 flagship, and p3.2xlarge is the single older V100 option.

questions.q: What do the Azure DSVM (ubuntu-hpc) image and the AWS Deep Learning AMI both provide out of the box?
options: A pre-configured Kubernetes device plugin for GPU scheduling
NVIDIA drivers and the CUDA Toolkit already installed on the image
A pre-provisioned MIG partition layout
A Terraform state file for the GPU VM
questions.explain: Both are Marketplace/AMI images that ship with GPU drivers and CUDA pre-installed, letting you skip the driver/CUDA bootstrap work covered in the next lesson.

questions.q: Why does a cluster of GPU VMs that need low-latency interconnect for distributed training often use a proximity placement group (Azure) or cluster placement group (AWS)?
options: To automatically install the NVIDIA Container Toolkit across the cluster
To qualify for a lower GPU quota requirement
To ensure the VMs land physically close together for low-latency networking between them
To enable Multi-Instance GPU partitioning across the VMs
questions.explain: Placement groups influence physical placement so that multiple GPU VMs end up close together on the provider's network, reducing interconnect latency for distributed training — a concern this course returns to later.
